input.title: Refund amount is never validated against captured amount
input.explanation: refund() accepts any amount and returns it as refunded without checking it against order.captured. A caller can refund more than was captured, including negative or non-finite values, which can lead to over-refunding customers and inconsistent ledger state. The function also performs no bounds checks at all, so the bug is not limited to a single edge case.
input.failureScenario: An order with captured = 50 is refunded with amount = 500. The function returns { refunded: 500 } and the caller pays out 500 against 50 captured. Passing a negative amount would similarly produce a negative refund.

fix.summary: Validate amount is finite, positive, and not greater than order.captured before returning the refund.

content.text:
I reported one finding for `src/refund.ts`, the most important bug in the file.

**Refund amount is never validated against the captured amount (critical, correctness).** `refund()` returns `{ refunded: amount }` without checking `amount` against `order.captured`. A refund larger than the captured amount goes through, and so do negative or non-finite values. The proposed patch throws a `RangeError` when the amount is not a positive finite number or when it exceeds `order.captured`.

The review covered only this file. I did not look at callers or tests, so the finding rests on the function body alone. The finding was recorded with confidence 0.9.
